prediction:
#13, the wide-line CAP rule.  Third registration: the deadband stands, and
the Fill_* leg is re-scoped because the device falsified its PREMISE.

WHAT THIS IS.  #13's extent phase landed exact and left ~908 px of
whole-capture coverage residual over the 48 non-void Line_* captures, 98.8% of
it within w/2 + 2 px of a vertex.  That class is the CAP.  The rule, derived
from the goldens with no fitted constant: the footprint never reaches past the
endpoints' own minor coordinates extended by w/2 -- the WIDTH, not the widened
extent E -- with both bounds rounded OUTWARD to whole pixel indices,

    minor index i is lit only if  floor(m_min - w/2) <= i <= ceil(m_max + w/2)

which turns the parallelogram into a hexagon where it bites.  On the ANALYTIC
MODEL (line_cap_phase.py --rivals, 48 captures, 1,967,133 golden ink px) it
scores 102 px against the unclipped footprint's 495, its nearest rival
floor + 1 scores 115, and the centre-sampled band 645.  On the shader's own
polygon rasterised at the device's 1/256 tie bias, 935 px -> 544.  The two are
DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS and must not be quoted into one sentence.

cap_clip() leaves the polygon untouched when it violates a plane by less than
HALF A GUEST PIXEL.  Derived, not tuned: the planes are whole pixel INDICES,
this renderer takes one sample per pixel at the pixel CENTRE, so the nearest
sample to a bound is half a pixel away at surface_scale_factor 1 and a
shallower cut removes none.  That is what the SECOND arm was about, and it
worked -- see below.

WHAT THE SECOND ARM SAID, AND THE ONE LEG THAT FIRED.
a_ref 28a3805b93 / b_ref 36e85c96c9, two runs a side, each byte-identical
with itself: 20 BETTER, 0 WORSE, 146 SAME.  N1 is closed on silicon -- the
eight captures at w = 4 to 14 that the pre-deadband arm made worse did not
move at all, and neither did the VOID captures.  The wide-end pair that the
last registration declined to defend, Line_0063.0 and Line_0063.1, came back
BETTER (-8 and -3).

One leg failed, and it was this file's: Line_width/Fill_* under
must_not_move, tripped by Fill_0032.0 going 26,721 -> 26,717.  Better.  Four
pixels, every one of them onto the golden's exact value, one of them from lit
cyan (54,252,252) to the golden's background (32,34,36) -- the cap clip's own
signature.

THE PREMISE WAS FALSE, NOT THE RESULT, and that is the only thing that makes
this re-scope legitimate.  This lane has twice refused to weaken a leg the
device broke.  Here the leg's stated reason -- "with widen_lines false the
generator emits the byte-identical fill shader it emitted before" -- is not
true of this capture.  SetFill() sets NV097_SET_FRONT_POLYGON_MODE, and a
polygon mode decides nothing for a LINE primitive:
pgraph_prim_rewrite_get_output_mode() maps LINE_LOOP to PRIM_TYPE_LINES
irrespective of polygon_mode, glsl/geom.c builds state->primitive_mode from
that output mode, and widen_lines is true for every PRIM_TYPE_LINES draw.
line_width_tests.cpp draws SIX blocks and the first is a 16-segment
LINE_LOOP, so a Fill_* capture is five filled blocks AND one wide line loop
at the suite's width (0, 1 and 32).  The capture was always reachable.

line_cap_phase.py --fills is the check this file rests on, and it is new
because every other mode there is blind to these captures: lp.captures()
matches Line_(\d+)\.(\d), so three of the suite's 61 captures were outside
--rivals, --controls, --shader, --vs-goldens, --quantise and --scale-cost
alike.  Four legs, all PASS on this tree:

  the goldens' whole dependence on LINE_WIDTH is the loop's:  Fill_0000.0 vs
  Fill_0032.0 differ in 12,021 px, ZERO of them outside the loop's own
  unclipped w = 32 footprint or the guest's printed label (59 px); the five
  filled blocks contribute nothing.  The mutant -- those five blocks in the
  loop's place -- leaves 23,311 px unexplained, so the leg is about the loop
  and not about a large mask.  0 cuts and 0 quantised px at w = 0 and w = 1;
  6 cuts at w = 32 (8 without the deadband), so the leg above is not vacuous.

LEG C1 -- THE CAP LEG, read by hand off arm B, not in `expect`.

  docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py --vs-goldens <armB captures>

PREDICTED: at most 600 mismatched px over the 48 non-void Line_* captures.
ARM A: ~908 px (extent fix, no cap clip).  FAILS IF: above 600 px.
The bound holds under either modelling of the tie -- 21 px and 544 px both

LEG C2 -- BIT-IDENTICAL BELOW THE DEADBAND'S REACH, the machine-read leg.
Below the deadband emit_line() emits master's four corners, in master's
order, with master's values: the widened path's only new geometry is the cut
vertex, and where the clip does not bite there is none.  So:

  Line_width/Line_0000.*, Line_0001.*, Line_000[3-9].0, Line_001[0-6].0
      every capture below w = 24.  Eight of these were WORSE on the FIRST
      arm; on the second, with the deadband, all of them held exactly.
  Line_width/Line_0064.*, Line_width/Line_FFFFFFFF
      VOID: the width register holds nine bits of eighths, 64.0 does not fit,
      hardware drew all nine at 1.0 and the device draws them at 1.0 too.
      Each moved 1,402 -> 1,401 on the first arm and held on the second.
  Line_width/Fill_0000.*, Line_width/Fill_0001.*
      the line loop at w = 0 and w = 1.  RE-SCOPED FROM Line_width/Fill_*.
      These are the half of the old glob the mechanism supports, and they are
      the DISCRIMINATING half: if the Fill_* captures moved for some reason
      other than the loop -- the geometry push-constant range, a pipeline
      layout, a shader-cache key -- all three would move together.  Both held

  Blend_tests/*
      the geometry push-constant range is declared on EVERY graphics
      pipeline, whether or not it has a geometry shader, so a mistake there
      shows up on a suite that draws no wide lines at all.

FAILS IF: any of them moves.  line_cap_phase.py --quantise is the offline
form of this leg and reads 0 quantised px moved after the deadband, against

LEG C4 -- Line_width/Fill_0032.0 = 26,717, IN `expect`.
The capture the old glob got wrong, on the improving side, at a value and not

WHAT IS NOT PREDICTED, AND WHY expect_counts IS STILL GONE.  The ~544 px

(1) 0.5 is half a GUEST pixel and the samples are DEVICE pixel centres, so it
